appliedUpdates.description: Updated .factory/library/re-platform.md MCP Server section: replaced '5 stub tools' with detailed descriptions of all implemented tools (decompile_binary, recompile_binary, classify_malware, ask_ai_about_binary, ai_code_reconstruction), documented remaining stub (generate_exploit), added dual-argument pattern documentation, and noted OllamaRepairEngine adapter and pipeline integration patterns.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add coding convention: 'Use asyncio.get_running_loop() instead of asyncio.get_event_loop() (deprecated in Python 3.10+) when running inside async contexts.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: mcp-decompile-binary worker replaced 3 instances of get_event_loop() with get_running_loop() in reveng_enterprise_server.py (analyze_binary, decompile_binary, find_vulnerabilities handlers).

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add coding convention: 'MCP tool handlers should accept both the canonical argument name and legacy aliases via the _resolve_binary_argument() helper for backward compatibility.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: All 4 mcp-tools features use _resolve_binary_argument() to accept both 'binary_path' (canonical) and 'path' (legacy). This pattern was independently adopted by all workers.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add boundary: 'Avoid calling private methods (underscore-prefixed) from other modules. If private engine methods are needed, add a public wrapper method to the engine class instead.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: mcp-recompile-binary worker calls engine._phase1_decompilation() and engine._compile_with_feedback_loop() (private methods of BinaryRecompilationEngine) directly from reveng_enterprise_server.py. This creates brittle coupling.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Clarify Ollama convention: 'When a feature description explicitly specifies an integration method (e.g., HTTP API), that takes precedence over the default AGENTS.md convention (use ollama Python package).'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: mcp-ai-query worker used direct HTTP requests.post to Ollama API as specified by feature description, while AGENTS.md says 'Use the ollama Python package when available.' mcp-recompile-binary used the ollama package. This inconsistency should be clarified.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: In python-developer skill step 4 ('Write tests first'), add exception: 'When replacing stub handlers that return hardcoded strings, you may implement the handler first to establish the return schema, then write tests against the real schema.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: mcp-ai-query worker deviated from TDD because existing handlers were pure stubs. Creating the real return shape first was more practical for writing stable tests.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Document the LLM adapter duck-typing interface: 'LLM adapters used by BinaryRecompilationEngine must implement _generate_async(prompt: str) -> str and is_available() -> bool methods, matching GeminiEngine's interface.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: mcp-recompile-binary worker created OllamaRepairEngine implementing _generate_async() and is_available() to duck-type GeminiEngine. This interface is not documented anywhere, making future LLM backend additions harder.
